facts.text: Crown Hill Cemetery began in 1863 during the Civil War, originally named Strawberry Hill before becoming “The Crown” for its lofty overlook of Indianapolis.
Located at 700 West 38th Street, Crown Hill is Indiana’s largest rural cemetery and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.
In 1970 the cemetery’s Waiting Station was leased for a dollar a year to the Historic Landmarks Foundation of Indiana, which restored the historic structure.
The Crown Hill Heritage Foundation, founded in 1984, raises money to preserve the cemetery’s historic buildings and beautiful grounds.
A docent‑led public tour at Crown Hill shares the cemetery’s history and the arboretum’s natural beauty, adding cultural context to the walk.
The Hearts Remembered Memorial, dedicated in 2006, honors Indianapolis’s orphaned children, many of whom were buried in unmarked graves.
